description:
Confidence-blocking finding from review: `apps/jido_connect_salesforce/test/jido_connect/salesforce/client_test.exs` uses randomized async tests with `function_exported?/3` checks but only one test explicitly calls `Code.ensure_loaded/1`. Under different seeds, different delegate checks fail even though `mix run` shows `Jido.Connect.Salesforce.Client.__info__(:functions)` includes the expected functions. Observed failures included `query_more/2`, `describe_object/2`, `update_lead/2`, and `update_task/2`.

Why this matters: this is probably a test-load-order problem rather than a production API omission, but it creates false negatives in the Salesforce package. False negatives are still damaging: they make the factory loop appear unreliable and can hide a real future delegate regression because maintainers stop trusting the test.

Acceptance:
- Make the Salesforce client delegate tests deterministic under randomized ExUnit seeds.
- Either ensure the module is loaded before each `function_exported?/3` check, collapse delegate checks into one loaded-module test, or assert via `Client.__info__(:functions)` after explicit load.
- Confirm the source still exports the expected public API: query, query_more, get/describe/list recent, create/update record, contact, lead, and task delegates.
- `cd apps/jido_connect_salesforce && mix test --no-deps-check` passes repeatedly with at least two explicit seeds, including one previously failing seed if available.
- Do not remove delegate coverage; make it trustworthy.
title: [REVIEW-S05] Make Salesforce client delegate tests deterministic
